question.text: Mr. Aditya Sharma, a lead angel investor, creates a syndicate 'AGS LLP' to raise INR 25 crore for a Pre-Series A in a FinTech start-up. He commits INR 5 crore himself and the other accredited investors commit INR 20 crore. Carry to the lead is 15%. Three years later the syndicate exits at INR 75 crore. What amount of carry does Mr. Sharma receive on the INR 50 crore profit?

answer.text: INR 11.25 crore (15% of INR 75 crore exit value)
INR 3.75 crore (15% of INR 25 crore initial capital)
INR 6.00 crore (15% of INR 40 crore non-lead capital)
INR 7.50 crore (15% of INR 50 crore profit)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the syndicate example in Ch 11.1.2, carry is charged on the profit (exit value minus committed capital): INR 75 cr − INR 25 cr = INR 50 cr profit. Carry = 15% × INR 50 cr = INR 7.50 crore. The balance INR 42.50 cr is distributed pro-rata to all syndicate investors including Mr. Sharma himself. The Trap: Option A confuses carry base (total exit, not profit). Option B applies the fee to committed capital as if it were a flat management fee. Option D excludes the lead's own commitment from the carry base, which is incorrect — carry is on total syndicate profit.
